resolution.note:
Both refuters killed every blocking finding, so the row stamps PASS:verify-refuted and this REVISE stays as the record. strategy_tie_in §4 (strategy-fidelity check) line 21: scope: This finding has already been filed and refuted. I checked each claim against the files.

1. **Already adjudicated.** `curriculum/evals/instances/ae101--exercise--fork-the-worktree.strategy.json` at HEAD holds the same finding: check_strategy_tie_in §4, L21, the same parenthetical, and the same fix hint to drop the artifact names. It carries `resolution: {settled: "refuted"}`. Both refuters killed it because it moves the strategy doc's boundary earlier than the doc puts it. The doc says nothing may name the pieces "before the M4 evidence is read", not "before diagnose-and-resend". The file has not changed on this point, so re-filing does not change the verdict.

2. **The rule's line is already behind the student.** `agents-102-core/strategy/content-strategy-agentic-engineering-101.md` L384 says the constraint is "nothing may name the three pieces before the M4 evidence is read". By `fork-the-worktree`, the student has read the M4 return through four beats in `learn-from-the-test.md`:
   - Start here (L23, "You walk in with the artefact")
   - `## Say what done-done means`, whose answer lands in the transcript (L27–35)
   - `[Lecture: Reading the return]` (L37)
   - `## Your mid-run worries hint at missing checks`, which tests the worry against the return (L39–46)

   Rule §4 at current wording (rule.js) only asks whether a draft front-runs the doc's own sequencing claim, and this one does not.

3. **L21 is not where the names first appear.** The module's student-facing `## What You'll Learn` (L16–18) already names "a verifier", and "the reference artefact + plan.md", at module open, before any M4 reading. `diagnose-and-resend.md`'s header ("What you build: a verifier, a reference, and a plan.md") also names all three before its own Phase 1 diagnosis. Both passed strategy review. Cutting L21 would not keep the reveal unspoiled, because the names already appear earlier in the module. The harm claimed has no counterfactual.

4. **The precedent is quoted wrong.** The 2026-08-14 cut at `learn-from-the-test.md` L144 removed a statement of roles: "the reference pins the goal, plan.md carries the state, the verifier runs the checks". That hands out the pattern, what each piece does and why. L21 is a list of logistics: what runs in which directory. It gives no function, pairing or best-practice framing. The strategy doc's concern is "never as a best-practices lecture"; each piece should earn its name by what it catches. An inventory that assigns no role does not do what that concern is about. Calling it "the identical failure" overstates it. It was also a different beat: the mid-run-worries opener, not this exercise.

On the scope lens, (a) fails and (c) applies in effect: a dated resolution on this exact finding is on file. (b), (d) and (e) do not rescue the finding. / harm: The finding fails on its own premise, the fix would change nothing, and the precedent it cites is about something else.

1. **The rule's condition is already met.** The strategy doc (agents-102-core/strategy/content-strategy-agentic-engineering-101.md:384) says: "nothing may name the three pieces **before the M4 evidence is read**." In learn-from-the-test.md the order is: done-done prompt, then [Lecture: Reading the return] at line 37 (where the M4 artefact is read), then the mid-run-worries beat, then Hooks always fire, then fork-the-worktree at line 50. So line 21 of fork-the-worktree.md comes after the evidence is read. The judge sees this and falls back on a note about reading-the-return that isn't in the rule. That note describes what that one lecture chooses to do. It doesn't extend the embargo to every later beat.

2. **Removing the names from line 21 changes nothing (harm-lens d).** The module's own What You'll Learn names all three pieces at the top of M5, before any exercise: line 17 "Build a verifier..." and line 18 "Assemble the reference artefact + plan.md". diagnose-and-resend.md also names all three in its header, before its Phase 1: line 17 "What you build: a verifier, a reference, and a plan.md". The student has seen the three nouns at least once before line 21 and sees them again straight after it. So the "reveal" the finding protects has already happened, and cutting line 21 hides nothing.

3. **The precedent is misread.** learn-from-the-test.md:144 cut a sentence that gave each piece its role ("the reference pins the goal, plan.md carries the state, the verifier runs the checks"). The cut reason was "handed out all three roles before the student had diagnosed anything." Line 21 names the files the module will produce inside a sentence about logistics. It assigns no roles and tells the student nothing about which failure each piece catches. Earning each piece by contrast (which failure it would have caught) is still left entirely to diagnose-and-resend. The judge calls the two "identical" and they aren't.

4. **Author check (harm-lens e).** `git blame -L 21,21` shows commit c8e2be0e7 by Antti Tevanlinna on 2026-08-25. That matches the maintainer note at learn-from-the-test.md:142: "`## Set up the worktree` moved into `exercises/fork-the-worktree.md` ... (2026-08-25, Antti-directed) ... the rationale (same-code-state ...) rides the exercise". This is the maintainer's own wording, moved deliberately. It is not drift.

5. **Harm (a/b).** No student ends up worse off. The claimed harm is the rule restated, and it applies to a position the rule doesn't cover. The student already expects a verifier, a reference and a plan.md from the module header they just read.
